entry: Brazilian-American mixed martial artist. Nunes competes in the women's bantamweight division of the [[Ultimate Fighting Championship|Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC)]], where she is a former UFC Women's Featherweight Champion and former two-time UFC Women's Bantamweight Champion. She is the only woman to become a two-division UFC champion, and in 2022 she was ranked first in the UFC women's pound-for-pound rankings. Many commentators consider her the greatest female mixed martial artist of all time.

Basidiomycete [[Fungus]] with a bright red cap covered in white warts, commonly called fly agaric. It is native to temperate and boreal forests of the [[Northern Hemisphere]], where it forms symbiotic relationships with trees such as pines and spruces, and it is now naturalized in the Southern Hemisphere. Its psychoactive compounds, including muscimol and ibotenic acid, can cause poisoning, though fatal poisonings are extremely rare. Parboiling reduces toxicity, and drying converts ibotenic acid into muscimol while retaining psychoactive effects. The name may derive from its historical use to kill flies. [[Carl Linnaeus]] described it in 1753 as *Agaricus muscarius*, and [[Jean-Baptiste Lamarck]] placed it in the genus *Amanita* in 1783. Since the [[Renaissance]] it has appeared in fairy tales, children's books and media such as Disney's *Fantasia* (1940). Claimed links to [[Santa Claus]], Viking berserkers and Vedic soma are disputed, as the evidence is sparse.

Deadly poisonous basidiomycete mushroom, known as the death cap. It is native to Europe, where it forms ectomycorrhizae with broadleaved trees such as [[Oak|oaks]], and it has spread to other regions with the cultivation of non-native [[Chestnut|chestnuts]] and [[Pine|pines]]. Its cap is usually greenish but varies in color, and the mushroom resembles edible species such as Caesar's mushroom, which increases the risk of accidental poisoning. Amatoxins are thermostable, so cooking or freezing does not reduce them. As little as half a mushroom can contain enough toxin to kill an adult, and the species is responsible for 90% of mushroom-related fatalities worldwide. Its principal toxin, α-amanitin, causes [[Liver|liver]] and [[Kidney|kidney]] failure. It may have killed [[Claudius|Roman Emperor Claudius]] in AD 54.

Genus of plants, *Amaranthus*, commonly called amaranths. Some species are known as pigweeds. Members are annual or perennial herbs with succulent, hollow stems that can reach 1 to 2.5 meters tall, and catkin-like clusters of densely packed flowers appear in summer or fall. The genus is cosmopolitan in tropical regions, and some species are cultivated as leaf vegetables, pseudocereals and ornamental plants. Amaranth originated as a crop in Central and South America, where the [[Aztecs]] and Incas ate its seeds and leaves. The seeds are gluten-free and high in [[Protein|protein]], at 16–18% by weight, and the leaves are rich in vitamins A and C. Other species are notorious agricultural weeds.

Genus of bulbous flowering plants native to the Western Cape of South Africa. Its best-known species, *Amaryllis belladonna*, bears stems of two to twelve funnel-shaped flowers, which may be white, pink or purple. Its common names include belladonna lily, Jersey lily and naked lady, and March lily in South Africa. Although it is called a lily, it is only distantly related to the true [[Lilium|lily]]. Like other members of its family, it contains toxic [[Alkaloid|alkaloids]]. [[Carl Linnaeus]] named the species in 1753, and the name derives from a shepherdess in [[Virgil|Virgil's]] pastoral poems and the Greek word for *to sparkle*. The common name *amaryllis* is mainly applied to cultivars of *Hippeastrum*, which are sold for indoor winter blooms.

Sun goddess in [[Japanese mythology]]. She is often considered the chief deity of the [[Shinto]] pantheon and is portrayed in the [[Kojiki]] (c. AD 712) and the *Nihon Shoki* (AD 720) as ruler of the heavenly realm Takamagahara. She is the mythical ancestress of the [[Imperial House of Japan]] through her grandson Ninigi. Along with the [[Moon|moon]] deity Tsukuyomi and the storm god Susanoo, she is one of the "Three Precious Children" of the creator god Izanagi. The name Amaterasu Ōmikami is thought to mean "The Great August Goddess Who Shines in Heaven." Her chief shrine, the Grand Shrine of Ise in Mie Prefecture, is one of Shinto's holiest sites and a major pilgrimage center.

Non-commercial use of specific radio frequencies, also called ham radio, for communication, experimentation, self-training and emergency service. The International Telecommunication Union (ITU) regulates the amateur service, and national governments issue licenses with unique call signs after an examination on radio theory and regulations. In 1927 a radio amateur was defined as a person with a purely personal aim and without pecuniary interest. Amateurs have been credited with discovering skywave propagation and with providing emergency communications. In 2011 the American Radio Relay League estimated that about 2 million people worldwide were active in the hobby. The term *ham* was originally a pejorative used by professional [[Telegraphy|telegraphers]] for poor [[Morse code]] senders.

Series of e-readers designed and marketed by [[Amazon (company)|Amazon]]. The first device was released in 2007, and early models used E Ink displays that simulate the appearance of ink on paper. Kindles download e-books, newspapers, magazines and audiobooks from the Kindle Store over wireless networks. As of March 2018, the store had over six million e-books available in the United States. Kindle has been central to the shift toward digital publishing, but Amazon's pricing disputes with publishers drew antitrust scrutiny.

Subsidiary of [[Amazon (company)|Amazon]] that provides [[Cloud computing|cloud computing]] services. It offers on-demand platforms and APIs on a metered, pay-per-use basis, including virtual computers that can be scaled up or down with demand. Its services are delivered from [[Data center|data centers]] around the world, and they free clients from managing hardware and operating systems. As of the first quarter of 2023, AWS held 31% of the cloud infrastructure market, against 25% for [[Microsoft]] Azure and 11% for [[Google|Google Cloud]], according to Synergy Research Group.

American multinational [[Conglomerate (company)|conglomerate]] engaged in e-commerce, retail, cloud computing and digital streaming. It was founded in 1994 by [[Jeff Bezos]] in Bellevue, Washington, as an online bookstore, and it expanded to sell most consumer products, positioning itself as *The Everything Store*. Subsidiaries include [[Amazon Web Services]] (AWS), [[Twitch (service)|Twitch]], IMDb and Whole Foods Market. It produces Kindle e-readers, Echo smart speakers and Fire tablets. In 2021 it surpassed [[Walmart]] as the world's largest retailer outside China. Its Amazon Prime subscription had 200 million subscribers worldwide. Critics have cited its surveillance partnerships, working conditions, anti-union efforts and censorship controversies, and in 2023 the U.S. Federal Trade Commission sued the company, alleging monopolistic tactics.

Freshwater toothed whale of the Amazon and [[Orinoco]] basins in South America, also called the boto or pink river dolphin. It is the largest river dolphin, and adults turn pink, more so in males. Males are 16% longer and 55% heavier than females. It eats up to 53 fish species, including [[Catfish|catfish]] and [[Piranha|piranhas]], as well as turtles and crabs. The International Union for Conservation of Nature ranked it endangered in 2018, with a declining population. Threats include fishing bycatch, hunting for bait, damming and pollution.

Female warriors and hunters in [[Greek mythology]]. In the myths, their society excluded men: they raised only daughters and returned sons to their fathers. The Amazons appear in the Labours of [[Heracles]], the *Argonautica* and the *Iliad*. Their homeland was placed variously in Asia Minor and the [[Eurasian Steppe|steppes]] around the [[Black Sea]], and most authors located their queen's capital, Themiscyra, in Pontus on the Thermodon river. Burials of female warriors among the [[Scythians|Scythian]] and Sarmatian peoples suggest that horse cultures inspired the myth. [[Herodotus]] wrote that Amazons intermarried with Scythians to form the Sauromatae.

Fossilized tree [[Resin|resin]], valued as a gemstone. It typically comes from ancient coniferous trees and has undergone polymerization and oxidation over millions of years. More than 150 types are recognized, grouped into five classes by chemical constituents. Because it began as soft, sticky resin, amber often preserves [[Insect|insects]], plant material and other inclusions. The most prolific deposits, Baltic amber from [[Eocene]] sediments about 44 million years old, have been used in jewelry since [[Neolithic]] times, and amber has been worked as a gemstone since classical antiquity. Its inclusions provide detailed evidence of prehistoric life.

Roman theologian, statesman and bishop of [[Milan]] from 374. Trained in rhetoric and law, he was governor of Aemilia-Liguria before he was acclaimed bishop. As bishop he defended Nicene orthodoxy against [[Arianism]], and he excommunicated [[Theodosius I]] after a massacre, insisting that "an emperor is within the church, not over it." His preaching helped convert [[Augustine of Hippo]] to Christianity. His writings include *De virginibus* (377) on virginity and *De officiis ministrorum* on the conduct of clergy, and he wrote at least four hymns, including "Veni redemptor gentium." He is one of the four original Western Doctors of the Church and is patron saint of Milan and beekeepers.

Vehicle equipped to transport patients to medical facilities, often providing care during transit. Most ambulances are built on [[Van|vans]] or pickup trucks, though some are motorcycles, buses, aircraft or boats. They respond to medical emergencies for [[Emergency medical services]] and carry paramedics and emergency equipment. The word derives from [[Latin]] *ambulare*, *to walk*, and originally meant a moving hospital that followed an army. Spanish forces first used ambulances for emergency transport in 1487, during the siege of Málaga. During the [[American Civil War]], wagons carrying wounded soldiers from the field were called ambulance wagons.

Emperor of Ethiopia (r. 1314–44) of the Solomonic dynasty. He is known mainly from *The Glorious Victories*, a Ge'ez chronicle of his 1332–1333 campaign against Ifat and Adal. Scholars disagree on its date: some regard it as a contemporary account, while Bertrand Hirsch proposes that it is a 15th-century epic that condenses about a century of conflict with the sultans of Ifat into his reign. Most of his wars were against [[Muslims|Muslim]] sultanates to the southeast, which he generally defeated, enlarging the kingdom by incorporating smaller states. His conquests extended Christian territory and power for centuries, and they supported the spread of [[Christianity]] to frontier areas. Edward Ullendorff called him "one of the most outstanding Ethiopian kings of any age."

Italian scientist known for molecular theory. Avogadro's law states that equal volumes of gases at the same temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of molecules. The hypothesis resolved discrepancies in combining volumes noted by [[Joseph Louis Gay-Lussac]] and helped distinguish atoms from molecules in gases. It gained wide acceptance only after Stanislao Cannizzaro highlighted it at the 1860 Karlsruhe Congress. The [[Avogadro constant]], 6.02214076×10²³ mol⁻¹, is named in his honor and is one of the seven defining constants of the [[International System of Units|SI]].

American aviation pioneer. In 1928 she became the first woman to cross the Atlantic by airplane, and in 1932 she made the first solo nonstop transatlantic flight by a woman, for which she received the Distinguished Flying Cross. She was one of the first aviators to promote commercial air travel, wrote best-selling books, and helped found the Ninety-Nines, an organization for women pilots. During an attempt to become the first woman to circumnavigate the world, she and navigator Fred Noonan vanished over the [[Pacific Ocean]] while flying toward [[Howland Island]]. Since then she has become a global cultural figure, the subject of numerous films and books.

Airline headquartered in [[Fort Worth, Texas|Fort Worth, Texas]]. It is the largest airline in the world by passengers carried and daily flights, operating almost 6,800 flights a day to nearly 350 destinations. Its largest hub is Dallas Fort Worth International Airport, and it serves more than 200 million passengers annually through its regional affiliates, which operate as American Eagle. It is a founding member of the oneworld alliance.

American breed of zebuine-taurine hybrid beef [[Cattle|cattle]]. It was bred in the United States from 1885 using cattle of Indian origin, imported at various times from India, Brazil and the United Kingdom, mainly Gir, Guzerá and Nelore stock. The breed has a high tolerance of heat, sunlight and humidity, and good resistance to parasites. It has been exported to many [[Tropics|tropical]] countries, and in Australia it is the most numerous breed of cattle. It has also been used to create taurine-indicine hybrids, such as the Brangus and Brahmousin, which are established as separate breeds.

Commercial television network owned by [[The Walt Disney Company|Disney]]. Known as ABC, it is the youngest of the "Big Three" American networks, with [[NBC]] and [[CBS]]. It began in 1943 as a radio network, succeeding the NBC Blue Network, and it extended to television in 1948. ABC merged with Capital Cities Communications in the 1980s, and the combined company merged into Disney in 1996. It has eight owned-and-operated stations and more than 230 affiliates in the United States. ABC is headquartered in Burbank, California.

Civil war in the United States, 1861–1865, between the Union and the Confederacy. Seven slave states seceded after the 1860 election of [[Abraham Lincoln]], a Republican who opposed the expansion of slavery, and they formed the [[Confederate States of America]]. The war began on April 12, 1861, when Confederate forces bombarded Fort Sumter. The Union captured [[New Orleans]] in 1861–62 and split the Confederacy at the [[Mississippi River]] with the siege of Vicksburg in 1863. The Emancipation Proclamation of January 1, 1863, made abolition a Union war goal and applied to more than 3.5 million of the 4 million enslaved people. Lee's incursion north failed at [[Battle of Gettysburg|Gettysburg]], and [[Robert E. Lee]] surrendered to [[Ulysses S. Grant]] on April 9, 1865. The Thirteenth Amendment abolished slavery, and the war was followed by the [[Reconstruction era]]. An estimated 700,000 soldiers died, the deadliest conflict in U.S. history.

Variety of [[English language|English]] native to the United States. English is the most widely spoken language in the country and the common language of government, education and commerce in all 50 states. American English differs from other varieties in pronunciation, [[Vocabulary|vocabulary]], [[Grammar|grammar]] and especially spelling. [[Noah Webster]] advocated spellings such as *color*, rather than *colour*. Any accent lacking noticeable local markers is called General American. Since the late 20th century, American English has been the most influential form of English worldwide.

1930 [[Oil painting|oil]] painting by Grant Wood. Painted on beaverboard, it shows a farmer holding a pitchfork beside a woman in an apron, in front of a Carpenter Gothic farmhouse in Eldon, Iowa. Wood modeled the figures on his sister Nan Wood Graham and on his dentist, Byron McKeeby. Some viewers have read the work as [[Satire|satire]] of rural Midwesterners, while Wood reportedly intended a celebratory portrayal of American values. The painting was made as the [[Great Depression]] began and is held by the [[Chicago|Art Institute of Chicago]]. It is frequently parodied.

American [[Reality television|reality]] singing competition. The series was created by Simon Fuller, based on the British series *Pop Idol*. It aired on Fox from 2002 to 2016 for 15 seasons and was revived on ABC in 2018. Winners were chosen by viewers through telephone and online [[Voting|voting]] from among unsigned singers. The original judging panel included [[Simon Cowell]], and [[Kelly Clarkson]] was the first winner. For eight consecutive seasons, from 2003–04 to 2010–11, either its performance or results show ranked first in U.S. television ratings.
